question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art of preparing, stuffing, and mounting the skins of dead animals so as to give them a lifelike appearance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Taxidermy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Taxidermy" means the art of preparing, stuffing, and mounting the skins of dead animals to give them a lifelike appearance, from the Greek “taxis” (arrangement) and “derma” (skin). (पशुओं को भरकर सुरक्षित रखने की कला)
◦ Example: The museum's taxidermy display included a lifelike stuffed tiger.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Embalming (शव लेपन): Treating a dead body with chemicals to preserve it from decay.

 

• Option 3: Mummification (ममीकरण): An ancient practice of preserving a body by embalming and wrapping it, as in Egypt.

 

• Option 4: Osteology (अस्थि विज्ञान): The scientific study of the structure and function of bones.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Taxidermy" frequently asked in SSC: Embalming (preserving a dead body with chemicals), Mummification (preserving a body by wrapping and drying, as in ancient Egypt), Preservation (keeping something from decay or damage) and Osteology (the study of bones).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than are needed

2. Laconic (अल्पभाषी): Using very few words to express oneself

3. Reticent (मितभाषी): Reluctant to speak openly about one's thoughts

4. Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative

5. Altruist (परोपकारी): A person unselfishly concerned for the welfare of others

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Having unlimited power; all-powerful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Omnipotent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Omnipotent" means having unlimited or very great power; all-powerful, from the Latin “omni” (all) and “potens” (powerful). (सर्वशक्तिमान)
◦ Example: Many religions describe God as omnipotent.

 

• The prefix "Omni-" always denotes all or every, and the rest of the word tells us what quality is possessed universally — power (omnipotent), knowledge (omniscient), presence (omnipresent), or food (omnivorous).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Omniscient (सर्वज्ञ): Having infinite knowledge or awareness of everything, from Latin “omni” (all) and “scire” (to know).

 

• Option 2: Omnipresent (सर्वव्यापी): Present everywhere at the same time, from Latin “omni” (all) and “praesens” (present).

 

• Option 4: Omnivorous (सर्वाहारी): Eating both plant and animal food, from Latin “omni” (all) and “vorare” (to devour).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "Omni-" words frequently asked in SSC: Omniscient (all-knowing), Omnipresent (present everywhere), Omnivorous (eating everything), Omnifarious (of all kinds), Omnificent (creating everything) and Omnibus (covering many things at once).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury and pleasure

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who generously helps others

3. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who hates or distrusts mankind

4. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान रूप से कुशल): Able to use both hands equally well

5. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of open spaces or crowded public places.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Agoraphobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Agoraphobia" means an abnormal fear of open spaces or crowded public places, from the Greek “agora” (marketplace/open space) and “phobos” (fear). (खुले स्थानों या भीड़ का भय)
◦ Example: Her agoraphobia made it difficult for her to visit crowded markets.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an intense or irrational fear, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from Latin “claustrum” (a closed place).

 

• Option 2: Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights, from Greek “akron” (summit/height).

 

• Option 3: Xenophobia (विदेशियों से भय या घृणा): A deep-rooted fear or dislike of foreigners or strangers, from Greek “xenos” (stranger).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Hydrophobia (water), Arachnophobia (spiders), Necrophobia (death or dead bodies), Photophobia (light), Nyctophobia (darkness) and Zoophobia (animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Iconoclast (परंपरा-भंजक): One who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

2. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place

3. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion

4. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders without a settled home

5. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Information that prematurely reveals crucial plot details of a film, show, or book.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Spoiler.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Spoiler" means information that prematurely reveals crucial plot details of a film, show, or book, ruining the surprise for the audience. (कथानक भेद)
◦ Example: He accidentally posted a spoiler about the movie's ending on social media.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Trailer (फिल्म का पूर्वावलोकन): A short preview or advertisement showing scenes from an upcoming film without revealing its ending.

 

• Option 3: Sequel (अगली कड़ी): A film, book, or show that continues the story of an earlier one.

 

• Option 4: Cameo (विशेष अतिथि भूमिका): A brief appearance by a well-known person in a single scene of a film or show.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Spoiler" frequently asked in SSC: Trailer (a preview of a film), Sequel (a continuation of a story), Prequel (a story set before the original), Cameo (a brief guest appearance) and Blooper (an embarrassing on-screen mistake).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Epicure (स्वादिष्ट भोजन-प्रेमी): A person devoted to fine food and drink

2. Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practices strict self-denial

3. Cynic (निंदक): A person who distrusts others' motives

4. Pedant (पंडिताऊ व्यक्ति): One overly concerned with minor rules or details

5. Zealot (कट्टरपंथी): A person fanatically devoted to a cause

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anagram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anagram" means a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase, from the Greek “ana” (again/back) and “gramma” (letter). (अक्षरों की उलट-फेर से बना शब्द)
◦ Example: "Listen" is an anagram of "silent".

 

• Words ending in "-gram" often relate to something written, drawn, or recorded, as in anagram (rearranged letters), telegram (a written message), and diagram (a drawn plan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Palindrome (उल्टा-सीधा एक समान पढ़ा जाने वाला शब्द): A word, phrase, or number that reads the same backward as forward, e.g., "madam".

 

• Option 3: Acronym (संक्षिप्ताक्षर): A word formed from the initial letters of a series of words, e.g., "NASA".

 

• Option 4: Homonym (समरूप भिन्नार्थक शब्द): A word that is spelled or pronounced the same as another word but has a different meaning.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Anagram" frequently asked in SSC: Palindrome (reads the same backward as forward), Acronym (formed from initial letters), Homonym (same spelling/sound, different meaning), Homophone (same sound, different spelling/meaning) and Synonym (same or similar meaning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier who fights for payment

2. Pacifist (शांतिवादी): A person who opposes war and violence

3. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with excessive, unreasoning patriotism

4. Egoist (अहंवादी): A person who thinks mainly of themselves

5. Altruist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes that pleasure is the most important thing in life and lives accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Hedonist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hedonist" means a person who believes that pleasure is the most important thing in life and lives for its pursuit, from the Greek “hedone” (pleasure). (सुखवादी)
◦ Example: As a confirmed hedonist, he spent his fortune on fine wine and travel.

 

• The suffix "-ist" here denotes a believer in or follower of a particular doctrine or way of life, as in hedonist (pleasure), pacifist (peace), and altruist (others' welfare).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Stoic (विपत्ति में अविचलित व्यक्ति): A person who endures pain and hardship without showing feelings or complaint, named after the Greek philosophy of Stoicism.

 

• Option 2: Puritan (कट्टर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views, especially regarding pleasure and self-indulgence.

 

• Option 4: Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practices severe self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Hedonist" frequently asked in SSC: Epicure (one who enjoys fine food and drink), Sybarite (one devoted to luxury), Sensualist (one absorbed in bodily pleasure), Ascetic (one who denies worldly pleasure) and Stoic (one indifferent to pleasure and pain).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The story of one's life written by oneself

2. Biography (जीवनी): The story of a person's life written by another

3. Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): Words inscribed on a tombstone

4. Eulogy (प्रशंसा भाषण): A speech praising someone, often the deceased

5. Elegy (शोकगीत): A mournful poem, especially for the dead

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who rejects all forms of government and political authority.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Anarchist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anarchist" means a person who believes in and advocates the abolition of all government and political authority, from the Greek “an-” (without) and “arkhos” (ruler). (अराजकतावादी)
◦ Example: The anarchist argued that all forms of government inevitably lead to oppression.

 

• The suffix "-ist" here denotes one who believes in or advocates a particular ideology; "Anarchist" is related to "Anarchy" (absence of government), just as "Autocrat" is related to "Autocracy".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Loyalist (राजभक्त): A person who remains loyal to the existing government or ruler, especially during a revolt.

 

• Option 2: Monarchist (राजतंत्र समर्थक): A person who supports rule by a monarch or royal family.

 

• Option 3: Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute power and governs without the consent of others, from Greek “autos” (self) and “kratos” (power).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words related in theme to "Anarchist" frequently asked in SSC: Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power), Bureaucracy (rule by officials), Democracy (rule by the people), Plutocracy (rule by the wealthy), Theocracy (rule by religious leaders) and Meritocracy (rule by the deserving).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Requiem (मृतकों के लिए शोक-संगीत): A hymn or mass for the dead

2. Panegyric (स्तुतिगान): A public speech praising someone highly

3. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श समाज): An imagined perfect society

4. Dystopia (दुःस्वप्निल समाज): An imagined society full of suffering

5. Nostalgia (अतीत की याद): A sentimental longing for the past

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is an expert in the scientific study of human behaviour and the mind.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Psychologist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Psychologist" means an expert in the scientific study of the human mind and behaviour, from the Greek “psyche” (mind/soul) and “logos” (study). (मनोवैज्ञानिक)
◦ Example: The psychologist helped the patient understand the root of his anxiety.

 

• The suffix "-logist" always denotes an expert or specialist in a particular field of study, and the first part of the word tells us that field — the mind (psychologist), society (sociologist), or humankind (anthropologist).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Psychiatrist (मनोरोग विशेषज्ञ): A medical doctor who diagnoses and treats mental illness, often through medication, from Greek “psyche” (mind) and “iatros” (healer).

 

• Option 3: Sociologist (समाजशास्त्री): An expert in the study of the development, structure, and functioning of human society.

 

• Option 4: Anthropologist (मानवविज्ञानी): An expert in the study of humankind, especially its origins, culture, and development.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logist/-ology" words frequently asked in SSC: Archaeologist (ancient remains), Entomologist (insects), Ornithologist (birds), Etymologist (word origins), Cardiologist (the heart) and Zoologist (animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Astrologer (ज्योतिषी): One who studies stars' supposed influence on humans

2. Numismatist (मुद्राशास्त्री): A collector or student of coins

3. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A collector of postage stamps

4. Entomologist (कीटविज्ञानी): An expert in the study of insects

5. Ornithologist (पक्षीविज्ञानी): An expert in the study of birds

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The category to which a creative work such as a film or series belongs, based on its style or content.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Genre.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Genre" means a category of artistic work, such as a film, book, or song, distinguished by a particular style, form, or content, from the French “genre”, ultimately from the Latin “genus” (kind/sort). (विधा/शैली)
◦ Example: Horror is her favourite genre of film.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Motif (आवर्ती भाव): A recurring image, idea, or theme that runs through a work of art or literature.

 

• Option 3: Theme (विषयवस्तु): The central topic, subject, or underlying message of a creative work.

 

• Option 4: Format (प्रारूप): The particular style, arrangement, or manner in which something is presented.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Genre" frequently asked in SSC: Motif (a recurring idea in a work), Theme (the central subject of a work), Format (the manner of presentation), Category (a class or division) and Style (a distinctive manner of expression).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bibliomaniac (पुस्तकों का अत्यधिक शौकीन): A person obsessively fond of collecting books

2. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की सनक वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

3. Pyromaniac (आगजनी की सनक वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive urge to start fires

4. Megalomaniac (आत्म-महत्व के भ्रम वाला व्यक्ति): A person obsessed with their own power

5. Astronaut (अंतरिक्ष यात्री): A person trained to travel in spacecraft

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who writes the script or screenplay for a film, television show, or play.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scriptwriter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Scriptwriter" means a person who writes the script or screenplay for a film, television programme, or play (a compound of "script" and "writer"). (पटकथा लेखक)
◦ Example: The scriptwriter revised the dialogue three times before the director approved it.

 

• The suffix "-writer" denotes a person who writes a particular kind of text, as in scriptwriter (screenplays), copywriter (advertising text), and ghostwriter (writing for someone else).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Director (निर्देशक): The person who oversees the creative and technical aspects of making a film or show.

 

• Option 2: Producer (निर्माता): The person responsible for financing and organizing the making of a film or show.

 

• Option 4: Editor (संपादक): The person who selects and assembles the recorded footage into the final version of a film.

 

NOTE

 

• Other film-industry words close in meaning to "Scriptwriter" frequently asked in SSC: Director (oversees the making of a film), Producer (finances a film), Cinematographer (handles the camera work), Choreographer (designs the dance sequences) and Editor (assembles the footage).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Aeronaut (वायुयात्री): A pilot or traveller in a balloon/airship

2. Cosmopolitan (विश्वजनीन): At ease in many countries and cultures

3. Patriot (देशभक्त): A person who loves and supports their country

4. Deserter (भगोड़ा सैनिक): A soldier who abandons duty without permission

5. Truant (बिना अनुमति स्कूल से अनुपस्थित छात्र): A student who stays away from school without leave

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A newly coined word or expression that has recently come into use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Neologism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Neologism" means a newly coined word, phrase, or expression that has recently entered use in a language, from the Greek “neo” (new) and “logos” (word). (नवशब्द)
◦ Example: "Selfie" was once a neologism but is now a standard English word.

 

• The prefix "Neo-" always denotes new or recent, as seen in words like neologism (a new word), neonatal (newborn), and neophyte (a beginner or new convert).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Jargon (विशेष शब्दावली): Special words or expressions used by a particular profession or group that are difficult for others to understand.

 

• Option 2: Slang (बोलचाल की अनौपचारिक भाषा): Very informal words and expressions more common in casual speech than in writing.

 

• Option 3: Colloquialism (बोलचाल का शब्द): A word or phrase used in ordinary, familiar conversation rather than formal speech or writing.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Neologism" frequently asked in SSC: Jargon (specialized professional vocabulary), Slang (very informal speech), Colloquialism (informal conversational usage), Archaism (an old, outdated word) and Idiom (a phrase with a non-literal meaning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Vegan (शुद्ध शाकाहारी): A person who eats no animal products

2. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats only plants

3. Carnivore (मांसाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats only meat

4. Teetotaler (पूर्ण मद्यत्यागी): A person who never drinks alcohol

5. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला व्यक्ति): A person who walks while asleep

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A large building used for housing and repairing aircraft.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hangar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hangar" means a large building used for housing, maintaining, or repairing aircraft (from the French "hangar", meaning a shed). (विमान रखने का शेड)
◦ Example: The new aircraft was towed into the hangar for inspection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Barn (खलिहान): A large farm building used for storing grain or housing livestock.

 

• Option 3: Warehouse (गोदाम): A large building used for storing goods and merchandise before distribution.

 

• Option 4: Silo (अनाज या मिसाइल भंडारण मीनार): A tall tower or pit used for storing grain, or an underground structure for housing a missile.

 

NOTE

 

• Other storage/building words close in meaning to "Hangar" frequently asked in SSC: Barn (a farm storage building), Warehouse (a goods storage building), Silo (a grain or missile storage tower), Depot (a storage or transport terminal) and Shed (a simple storage structure).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Insomnia (अनिद्रा): Habitual inability to sleep

2. Amnesia (स्मृतिलोप): Partial or total loss of memory

3. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): A person who copies another's work as their own

4. Forger (जालसाज़): A person who makes fraudulent copies or documents

5. Impostor (छद्मवेशी धोखेबाज़): A person who pretends to be someone else

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who dishonestly pretends to have medical knowledge or skill that they do not possess.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quack.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Quack" means a person who dishonestly pretends to have medical knowledge or skill that they do not actually possess, originally short for the Dutch "quacksalver" (one who boasts of remedies). (नीम-हकीम/जाली चिकित्सक)
◦ Example: The village quack prescribed the wrong medicine and worsened her illness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Charlatan (पाखंडी विद्वान): A person who falsely claims to have special knowledge or skill in any field, not necessarily medicine.

 

• Option 3: Impostor (छद्मवेशी धोखेबाज़): A person who deceives others by pretending to be someone else.

 

• Option 4: Swindler (धोखेबाज़): A person who cheats others out of money or property through deception.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Quack" frequently asked in SSC: Charlatan (a fraud who claims false expertise), Impostor (one who pretends to be someone else), Swindler (one who cheats others of money), Sycophant (one who flatters for gain) and Hypocrite (one who pretends to have virtues they lack).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others for personal gain

2. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी व्यक्ति): A shy person who focuses on inner thoughts

3. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी व्यक्ति): An outgoing, socially confident person

4. Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats or drinks excessively

5. Miser (कंजूस): A person who hoards money and avoids spending

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art or science of measuring time and of making clocks and watches.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Horology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Horology" means the art or science of measuring time and of making clocks, watches, and other timepieces, from the Greek “hora” (hour/time) and “logos” (study). (कालमापन विद्या/घड़ी विज्ञान)
◦ Example: The museum's horology exhibit displayed antique pocket watches and mechanical clocks.

 

• The suffix "-logy" always denotes the study or science of something, and the first part of the word tells us the subject — time (horology), the stars' influence (astrology), or the universe (cosmology).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Chronology (कालक्रम): The arrangement of events or dates in the order in which they occurred, from Greek “chronos” (time).

 

• Option 2: Astrology (ज्योतिष विद्या): The study of the positions and movements of celestial bodies believed to influence human affairs.

 

• Option 4: Cosmology (ब्रह्मांड विज्ञान): The scientific study of the origin, structure, and development of the universe.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logy" words frequently asked in SSC: Chronology (the order of events in time), Astrology (celestial influence on human affairs), Cosmology (the origin and structure of the universe), Etymology (the origin of words), Genealogy (family descent) and Mythology (traditional myths and legends).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys property

2. Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): Government conducted through officials, often rigidly

3. Democracy (लोकतंत्र): Government by the people, directly or through representatives

4. Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government controlled by the wealthy

5. Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government ruled by religious leaders or law

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An irrational and intense fear of flying.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Aerophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aerophobia" means an irrational and intense fear of flying, from the Greek “aer” (air) and “phobos” (fear). (हवाई यात्रा या उड़ने का भय)
◦ Example: Her aerophobia made it impossible for her to board the plane.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an irrational fear, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An irrational fear of heights, from the Greek “akron” (summit, peak).

 

• Option 2: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from the Latin “claustrum” (a closed space).

 

• Option 3: Agoraphobia (खुले स्थानों का भय): An irrational fear of open or crowded public spaces, from the Greek “agora” (marketplace).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Xenophobia (foreigners or strangers), Claustrophobia (enclosed spaces), Acrophobia (heights), Agoraphobia (open or crowded spaces), Hydrophobia (water), Nyctophobia (darkness), Arachnophobia (spiders) and Photophobia (light).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Misanthrope (मानव द्वेषी): One who hates or distrusts mankind

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): One who works for the welfare of others through donations

3. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

4. Numismatist (मुद्रा विज्ञानी): One who studies or collects coins

5. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): One who collects postage stamps

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The person who supervises and controls the making of a film.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Director.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Director" means the person who supervises and controls the making of a film, from the Latin “dirigere” (to direct, to guide). (निर्देशक)
◦ Example: The director insisted on reshooting the climax scene three times.

 

• The suffix "-or" in words like director, producer, and editor generally denotes a person who performs a particular role or action, a pattern common in profession-related SSC vocabulary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Producer (निर्माता): The person who finances, organises, and manages the overall production of a film.

 

• Option 3: Editor (संपादक): The person who cuts, arranges, and assembles the recorded footage into the final film.

 

• Option 4: Cinematographer (छायाकार): The person responsible for the camera work and lighting/visual style of a film.

 

NOTE

 

• Other film-related roles frequently asked in SSC: Producer (finances and manages a film), Screenwriter (writes the script), Cinematographer (handles camera and lighting), Choreographer (designs dance movements), Editor (assembles the final cut) and Dubbing artist (provides a character's voice).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Cartographer (मानचित्रकार): A person who draws or makes maps

2. Choreographer (नृत्य रचनाकार): One who designs and arranges dance movements

3. Calligrapher (सुलेखक): A person skilled in decorative handwriting

4. Orator (वाग्मी): A skilled and eloquent public speaker

5. Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person skilled in several languages or in linguistics

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The study of language in written historical sources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Philology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Philology" means the study of language in written historical sources, tracing its structure and development, from the Greek “philos” (loving) and “logos” (word, speech). (भाषा और साहित्य का ऐतिहासिक अध्ययन)
◦ Example: She pursued philology to trace how Sanskrit influenced modern Indian languages.

 

• The suffix "-logy" always denotes the study of a subject, and the first part of the word tells us what is studied.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Etymology (व्युत्पत्ति विज्ञान): The study of the origin and historical development of words, from the Greek “etymon” (true sense).

 

• Option 3: Linguistics (भाषा विज्ञान): The scientific study of language and its structure, without a specific historical focus.

 

• Option 4: Lexicography (शब्दकोश-निर्माण विज्ञान): The practice and art of compiling and editing dictionaries.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logy" words frequently asked in SSC: Etymology (origin of words), Anthropology (human societies and culture), Archaeology (ancient human history through artefacts), Genealogy (family ancestry), Etiology (causes of disease), Mythology (myths and legends) and Theology (religion and divine matters).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ornithologist (पक्षी विज्ञानी): One who studies birds

2. Entomologist (कीट विज्ञानी): One who studies insects

3. Archaeologist (पुरातत्वविद्): One who studies human history through excavation

4. Genealogist (वंशावली विशेषज्ञ): One who studies family ancestry and history

5. Herpetologist (सरीसृप एवं उभयचर विज्ञानी): One who studies reptiles and amphibians

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who offers to do something, especially work for others, without being paid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Volunteer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Volunteer" means a person who offers to do something, especially to work for others, without being paid, from the Latin “voluntarius” (willing), derived from “voluntas” (will). (स्वयंसेवक)
◦ Example: Hundreds of volunteers helped distribute relief material after the floods.

 

• Words built on the Latin root "volunt-" (will) include voluntary (done willingly) and involuntary (done unwillingly).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier hired to fight for a foreign power purely for financial gain, not out of loyalty or belief.

 

• Option 2: Freelancer (स्वतंत्र पेशेवर): A self-employed person who offers services to multiple clients or employers for payment.

 

• Option 4: Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who promotes the welfare of others, typically by donating money to good causes.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Volunteer" frequently asked in SSC: Philanthropist (one who donates for others' welfare), Altruist (one who is unselfishly concerned for others), Samaritan (a person who selflessly helps others in distress), Benefactor (one who gives financial help) and Humanitarian (one who works for human welfare).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Samaritan (भला मददगार): A charitable person who helps strangers in distress

2. Benefactor (उपकारी/दाता): A person who gives financial or other help

3. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders with no fixed home

4. Itinerant (घुमंतू): Travelling from place to place, especially for work

5. Wayfarer (पथिक): A traveller, especially one on foot

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An animal that lives both on land and in water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Amphibian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Amphibian" means an animal that can live both on land and in water, from the Greek “amphi” (both) and “bios” (life). (उभयचर)
◦ Example: The frog is a well-known amphibian that begins life in water as a tadpole.

 

• The prefix "amphi-" always denotes on both sides or of both kinds, as also seen in the word amphitheatre (seating on all sides).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reptile (सरीसृप): A cold-blooded, egg-laying animal with scaly skin that crawls or moves on short legs, such as a snake or lizard.

 

• Option 2: Crustacean (कवचधारी जलजीव): An aquatic animal with a hard outer shell and jointed limbs, such as a crab, prawn, or lobster.

 

• Option 3: Mammal (स्तनपायी): A warm-blooded animal that gives birth to live young and nourishes them with milk.

 

NOTE

 

• Other animal-classification words frequently asked in SSC: Reptile (cold-blooded, egg-laying land animal), Mammal (warm-blooded, milk-feeding animal), Aquatic (living in water), Herbivore (plant-eating animal), Carnivore (flesh-eating animal) and Omnivore (animal that eats both plants and flesh).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nocturnal (रात्रिचर): Active mainly during the night

2. Diurnal (दिनचर): Active mainly during the day

3. Migratory (प्रवासी): Moving from one region to another with the seasons

4. Carnivorous (मांसाहारी): Feeding on the flesh of other animals

5. Herbivorous (शाकाहारी): Feeding only on plants

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who practises strict self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence, usually for religious reasons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ascetic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ascetic" means a person who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence, often for religious reasons, from the Greek “asketes” (monk), derived from “askein” (to exercise, to train). (तपस्वी)
◦ Example: The ascetic lived in a Himalayan cave, surviving on fruits and water alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes that the pursuit of pleasure is the highest good in life.

 

• Option 3: Epicure (स्वाद-पारखी): A person who takes particular delight in fine food and drink.

 

• Option 4: Sybarite (विलासप्रिय): A person who is excessively fond of luxury, comfort, and pleasure.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Ascetic" frequently asked in SSC: Hermit (one who lives in solitude, often for religious reasons), Recluse (one who withdraws from society), Stoic (one who endures hardship without complaint), Puritan (one with strict moral views) and Anchorite (a religious recluse).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

2. Cosmopolitan (विश्वजनीन): A person who feels at home in all parts of the world

3. Connoisseur (कला-पारखी): A person with expert knowledge and taste in a fine art

4. Stoic (अविचलित/धैर्यवान): A person who endures hardship without complaint

5. Puritan (अतिशुद्धतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person, typically an artist or writer, who lives an unconventional and informal lifestyle, disregarding conventional social norms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bohemian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Bohemian" means a person, typically an artist or writer, who lives an unconventional and informal lifestyle disregarding social norms, originally applied in French to the Romani people, who were mistakenly believed to have come from Bohemia. (रूढ़िमुक्त जीवनशैली अपनाने वाला व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: She led a bohemian life in Paris, sharing a small studio with fellow painters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person belonging to a community that moves from place to place with no permanent home, typically for grazing livestock or trade.

 

• Option 3: Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place without a settled home or job, often idly.

 

• Option 4: Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An unorthodox or independent-minded person who does not conform to a group's views.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Bohemian" frequently asked in SSC: Maverick (unorthodox and independent), Nonconformist (one who does not conform to accepted norms), Iconoclast (one who attacks cherished beliefs), Eccentric (one with unconventional or odd habits) and Vagabond (a wanderer without a fixed home).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी): A shy, reserved person who prefers solitude

2. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी): An outgoing, socially confident person

3. Ambivert (उभयमुखी): A person having both introvert and extrovert traits

4. Pragmatist (व्यवहारवादी): A person who deals with things practically

5. Idealist (आदर्शवादी): A person guided by ideals rather than practicality

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A system of government in which one person possesses unlimited power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Autocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autocracy" means a system of government in which one person holds unlimited power, from the Greek “autos” (self) and “kratos” (power, rule). (एकतंत्र/निरंकुश शासन)
◦ Example: Historians describe the Tsarist regime as a classic autocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes a form of government or rule, and the first part of the word tells us who holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): A system of government in which power is vested in the people, exercised directly or through elected representatives.

 

• Option 2: Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): A government or state ruled by a privileged elite or hereditary nobility.

 

• Option 4: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): A system of government in which religious leaders rule in the name of God or a deity.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Democracy (rule by the people), Plutocracy (rule by the wealthy), Bureaucracy (rule by government officials), Theocracy (rule by religious leaders), Aristocracy (rule by the nobility) and Gerontocracy (rule by the elderly).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Despot (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler with absolute, often oppressive, power

2. Tyrant (अत्याचारी शासक): A cruel and oppressive ruler

3. Usurper (सत्ता हड़पने वाला): One who seizes power or a throne unlawfully

4. Regicide (राजहत्या): The killing of a king

5. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): One who believes in the abolition of all government

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A government ruled by the rich.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Plutocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Plutocracy" means a government or society ruled or controlled by people of great wealth, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth) and “kratos” (power, rule). (धनिकतंत्र)
◦ Example: Critics argue that unchecked corporate influence is turning the country into a plutocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes a form of government or rule, and the first part of the word tells us who holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Oligarchy (अल्पतंत्र): A government ruled by a small group of powerful people, often for their own benefit.

 

• Option 2: Kleptocracy (चोरतंत्र): A government whose rulers use their power to steal the country's wealth and resources.

 

• Option 3: Meritocracy (योग्यतातंत्र): A system in which power and status are given to people based on their talent and ability.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Autocracy (rule by one person), Democracy (rule by the people), Bureaucracy (rule by government officials), Theocracy (rule by religious leaders), Oligarchy (rule by a small group) and Meritocracy (rule based on ability).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Chauvinist (अंध राष्ट्रभक्त): One showing excessive, biased loyalty to one's own group

2. Bigot (पूर्वाग्रही व्यक्ति): A person intolerant of opinions differing from their own

3. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A fanatically committed follower of a cause

4. Fanatic (कट्टरपंथी): A person with excessive and uncritical enthusiasm

5. Renegade (विद्रोही/धर्मत्यागी): One who deserts a party or cause for another

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A group of people who travel with an important or famous person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Entourage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Entourage" means a group of people who travel with or attend an important or famous person, from the French “entourer” (to surround). (अनुचरवर्ग/साथ चलने वाला दल)
◦ Example: The film star arrived at the airport with a large entourage of assistants and bodyguards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Delegation (प्रतिनिधिमंडल): A group of representatives sent to a conference or authorised to act on behalf of others.

 

• Option 3: Contingent (टुकड़ी): A group of people, often representing a country or organisation, forming part of a larger gathering or force.

 

• Option 4: Convoy (काफिला): A group of vehicles, ships, or people travelling together, often for mutual protection.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Entourage" frequently asked in SSC: Retinue (attendants of an important person), Delegation (a group of official representatives), Contingent (a representative group within a larger body), Cavalcade (a procession of vehicles or riders) and Convoy (vehicles travelling together for protection).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Cavalcade (जुलूस): A procession of riders, vehicles, or ships

2. Retinue (अनुचरगण): A group of attendants accompanying an important person

3. Posse (सशस्त्र दल): A group organised to search for or pursue someone

4. Coterie (मित्र-मंडली): A small, exclusive group with shared interests

5. Cortege (शवयात्रा): A solemn procession, especially at a funeral

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who talks a great deal, especially about trivial matters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Garrulous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Garrulous" means excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters, from the Latin “garrulus” (talkative), derived from “garrire” (to chatter). (बातूनी/वाचाल)
◦ Example: The garrulous old man kept the entire bus entertained with his stories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reticent (मितभाषी): Not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reserved in speech.

 

• Option 3: Taciturn (मौन प्रकृति का): Reserved and saying very little; habitually silent by nature.

 

• Option 4: Eloquent (वाक्पटु): Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing, though not necessarily talkative.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Garrulous" frequently asked in SSC: Loquacious (very talkative), Voluble (speaking fluently and at length), Verbose (using more words than needed) and Chatty (fond of casual conversation). Their opposites — Reticent, Taciturn, and Laconic — describe a person who speaks very little.

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Loquacious (बातूनी): Tending to talk a great deal

2. Voluble (धाराप्रवाह बोलने वाला): Speaking fluently, readily, and at length

3. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than are needed

4. Laconic (अल्पभाषी): Using very few words; concise to the point of curtness

5. Ambiguous (द्विअर्थी): Open to more than one interpretation; unclear
